seo.title: Agent Workspace for Lawyers: Legal Workflows | Floatboat
seo.description: An AI agent workspace for lawyers to organize matter files, prepare legal research, compare documents, build timelines, and create reviewable legal drafts.

hero.eyebrow: A configurable AI workspace for legal work
hero.title: An AI agent workspace for lawyers and legal teams
hero.description: Floatboat works around your matters: organizing files, tracing facts, comparing versions, preparing research, and turning source material into reviewable drafts. You provide the playbook, templates, and approval points.

burdens.title: Legal judgment is only one part of the day.
burdens.description: Before a lawyer can advise, negotiate, or decide, someone has to recover context, organize materials, compare documents, and prepare a usable work product.

items.label: Files
items.title: Matter context is scattered
items.description: Important facts sit across folders, email attachments, meeting notes, prior drafts, and naming systems that drift over time.

items.label: Review
items.title: Every version creates more work
items.description: Teams must locate changes, reconnect them to the issue list, and explain what still needs a decision.

items.label: Research
items.title: Sources need more than a summary
items.description: Research has to be organized around the actual question, jurisdiction, date, and authority—not merely condensed.

items.label: Delivery
items.title: Clients need a clear next step
items.description: The internal analysis still has to become a concise update, meeting brief, request list, or editable draft.

workflows.title: Examples that adapt to your practice—not fixed legal playbooks.
workflows.description: Each workflow begins with materials and rules you control, produces an inspectable work product, and stops where professional judgment begins.

items.title: Turn a folder into a working matter brief
items.job: Recover the people, events, dates, missing material, and next questions before a meeting or handoff.
items.output: Chronology, document index, open questions, and an editable brief.
items.boundary: Floatboat organizes the record. Counsel decides relevance, privilege, strategy, and what may be shared.

items.title: Prepare a review queue from your own standards
items.job: Compare versions or check a document against the template, checklist, and issue categories supplied by your team.
items.output: Version summary, extracted terms, deviations, and unresolved questions.
items.boundary: The workspace surfaces differences and prepares questions; it does not make a final legal-risk determination.

items.title: Build a source trail before drafting the answer
items.job: Break a question into research issues, organize supplied or public sources, and prepare a traceable research packet.
items.output: Research log, authority matrix, unresolved conflicts, and a memo outline.
items.boundary: Every authority, quotation, jurisdictional assumption, and legal conclusion requires lawyer verification.

customization.title: Bring the standards your team already trusts.
customization.description: Different firms, clients, matters, and jurisdictions require different workflows. Floatboat should follow your approved materials and return decisions to the right person.

boundaries.title: Automate preparation, not professional responsibility.
boundaries.description: The useful line is not legal versus non-legal work. It is the line between preparing an inspectable work product and making a consequential professional decision.
assists: Matter indexes, chronologies, and source maps
Meeting briefs, client-update drafts, and request lists
Research packets, outlines, and editable first drafts
Recurring status summaries from approved materials

boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose agent workspace, not a law firm, legal research authority, or substitute for qualified legal counsel. Data handling depends on the models, tools, connectors, permissions, and organizational policies selected for each workspace.

faq.title: AI workspace questions for lawyers
faq.description: The practical questions are about source material, review, confidentiality, and control—not promises of one-click legal work.

items.question: Is Floatboat legal AI or a law-practice management system?
items.answer: Floatboat is a general-purpose Agent Workspace. It can help legal professionals work with approved files, research materials, templates, and repeatable preparation steps, but it is not a legal authority, matter-management system, billing platform, or substitute for counsel.

items.question: Can Floatboat review a contract?
items.answer: It can extract terms, compare versions, apply a checklist or template you provide, and prepare deviations and questions for review. A lawyer still determines legal meaning, risk, negotiation position, and whether any recommendation is appropriate.

items.question: Can it do legal research without hallucinations?
items.answer: No AI system should be treated as incapable of error. Floatboat can help structure research, organize sources, and create a traceable packet, but every authority, quotation, jurisdictional assumption, and conclusion must be verified against authoritative sources.

items.question: Does Floatboat come with a built-in law-firm playbook?
items.answer: The page examples are starting points, not prescribed legal methods. You choose the files, templates, checklists, terminology, output format, and approval steps appropriate to your firm, client, matter, and jurisdiction.

items.question: Can I use my own templates and checklists?
items.answer: Yes. A workspace can be organized around the materials and instructions you approve, so the agent prepares work in the structure your team expects instead of inventing a generic format.

items.question: How should privileged or confidential material be handled?
items.answer: Follow your firm's policies and client obligations before adding sensitive material. Review the data handling of every model, connector, and tool used in the workflow, scope access narrowly, and do not assume that local file access means every processing step remains on-device.

items.question: Will Floatboat send client messages or file documents automatically?
items.answer: The recommended workflows keep consequential external actions behind explicit human approval. Whether a connector can perform an action is separate from whether your policy should permit it.

items.question: Who is this page for?
items.answer: The examples are relevant to lawyers, in-house counsel, paralegals, legal operations teams, and other legal professionals who spend time preparing files, context, drafts, and repeatable work products.

finalCta.title: Give the work around legal judgment a better workspace.
finalCta.description: Start with a bounded folder, a trusted template, and a deliverable you can review. Keep the useful process; keep the professional decision yours.
